title: Establishment of a Spontaneous Ventilation Anesthesia Model for Beagle Dogs
author: Zeng, Liu, et al.

steps.title: Fast and water‑deprive dogs
steps.instruction: With healthy beagles weighing 12.0 ± 1 kg, withhold food from 22:00 the night before and remove water; begin the experiment about 10 h later.

steps.title: Induce anesthesia with propofol
steps.instruction: Place a catheter into the left forelimb radial vein and inject propofol 3–4 mg kg⁻¹. If needed, give an additional 2–3 mg kg⁻¹ based on the animal’s reaction.

steps.title: Position and secure the dog
steps.instruction: Lay the dog in supine position, secure it to a conventional large‑animal operating table, band the limbs and maxillofacial region with elastic bandages, and prepare the skin.

steps.title: Intubate and set ventilation
steps.instruction: Perform endotracheal intubation using a No. 7 single‑lumen tube, confirm placement with an electronic fiber bronchoscope, secure the tube with a bandage, connect the ECG monitor and ventilator circuit, and set synchronized intermittent mandatory ventilation (SIMV) with tidal volume 12 mL kg⁻¹, respiratory rate 20 min⁻¹, I:E ratio 1:1.5, and FiO₂ 100 %.

substeps.instruction: Confirm tube position using fiber bronchoscope
Set SIMV: tidal volume 12 mL kg⁻¹, RR 20 min⁻¹, I:E 1:1.5, FiO₂ 100 %

steps.title: Insert arterial line and femoral catheter
steps.instruction: Puncture the left femoral artery, insert a No. 20 single‑lumen catheter, attach a pressure transducer, and record invasive arterial blood pressure.

steps.title: Place jugular central line
steps.instruction: Puncture the right external jugular vein and insert a No. 20 single‑lumen central venous catheter for infusion.

substeps.instruction: Insert No. 20 single‑lumen central venous catheter

steps.title: Maintain anesthesia with infusions
steps.instruction: Run continuous infusions of propofol 2–5 mg kg⁻¹ h⁻¹, remifentanil 0.05–0.1 µg kg⁻¹ min⁻¹, epinephrine 0.1–0.2 µg kg⁻¹ min⁻¹, and norepinephrine 0.1–0.3 µg kg⁻¹ min⁻¹, adjusting rates according to the dog’s response.

steps.title: Monitor depth and give analgesic
steps.instruction: An anesthesiologist monitors sedation and analgesia depth; administer flurbiprofen 10 mg intravenously if additional analgesia is required.

steps.title: Switch to autonomous breathing
steps.instruction: After breathing rate and blood oxygen levels stabilize, stop ventilator‑assisted breathing, switch to autonomous breathing mode while keeping the dog connected to the ventilator, and continuously monitor airway resistance.

steps.title: Apply local intercostal lidocaine block
steps.instruction: Inject 5 mL of 1 % lidocaine stock solution for a local intercostal block.

steps.title: Perform right thoracotomy and insert sleeve
steps.instruction: Make a 2.5 cm incision on the right fifth intercostal space, then insert a protective sleeve into the incision.

substeps.instruction: Incise 2.5 cm at right fifth intercostal space

steps.title: Spray lidocaine on lung surface
steps.instruction: Spray 5 mL of 1 % lidocaine stock solution onto the exposed lung surface.

steps.title: Block intercostal nerves with lidocaine/ropivacaine
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1:1 mixture of 2 % lidocaine and 0.75 % ropivacaine; inject 1 mL of this solution into each of the 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, and 7th intercostal nerves (ropivacaine provides 4–6 h analgesia).
